flagged_sentences: JunJie Wu’s 2000 study in the American Journal of Agricultural Economics examined county-level data across the central United States and found that for every 100 acres enrolled in CRP, roughly 20 acres of non-cropland were converted to crops.

claims.claim: JunJie Wu's 2000 study found that for every 100 acres enrolled in CRP in the central United States, roughly 20 acres of non-cropland were converted to crops, offsetting 9% of water-erosion benefits and 14% of wind-erosion benefits.
claims.source_title: Slippage Effects of the Conservation Reserve Program
claims.supporting_quote: for each 100 acres of cropland retired under the CRP in the central United States, about 20 acres of non-cropland were converted to cropland; it quantifies that this slippage offsets roughly 9% of the CRP's water-erosion reduction benefits and 14% of its wind-erosion reduction benefits.

claims.claim: Shinsuke Uchida's 2011 paper found that an average partial-farm CRP participant converts 25% of noncropland to cropping activities as a consequence of CRP enrollment.
claims.source_title: Evaluation of the Conservation Reserve Program: Disaggregate slippage
claims.supporting_quote: it finds that an average partial-farm CRP participant converts 25% of noncropland to cropping activities as a consequence of CRP enrollment

claims.claim: Shinsuke Uchida's 2014 working paper estimated that an average CRP program participant converts 14% of noncropland to cropping activities after enrollment.
claims.source_title: Indirect Land Use Effects of Conservation: Disaggregate Slippage in the U.S. Conservation Reserve Program
claims.supporting_quote: It is found that an average program participant converts 14% of noncropland to cropping activities after enrollment.
